extra.message: JWT Signature Verification Disabled in insecure_verify — Authentication bypass: an attacker can forge arbitrary JWT tokens to access any customer's data via /get/<cust_id> without valid credentials [verified: insecure_verify calls jwt.decode(token, verify=False) disabling signature verification entirely; any token is accepted by /get/<cust_id>.]

Server-Side Template Injection via 404 Handler URL — Remote code execution on the server, full server compromise, data exfiltration [verified: request.url is interpolated into the template string via % formatting before render_template_string evaluates it; no auth required, no sanitization.]

Cleartext password storage in /register/customer — Attacker with database access (e.g. via SQL injection) obtains plaintext customer credentials [verified: Customer passwords stored as plaintext (content['password'] directly) with no hashing whatsoever in /register/customer.]

SQL Injection in Customer Search — Full read access to all database tables (customer PII, credit card numbers, user credentials with MD5 hashes), potential file read via SQLite ATTACH DATABASE, data modification or deletion [verified: content['search'] is directly string-interpolated into an SQL query with no parameterization or escaping; requires JWT auth but auth is freely available.]

Unsafe YAML Deserialization via yaml.load — Remote code execution: an attacker can execute arbitrary shell commands or Python code on the server [verified: yaml.load() on uploaded file content permits arbitrary Python object instantiation; no safe_load, no auth required.]

Weak Password Storage Using Unsalted MD5 — Compromise of user credentials if the SQLite database is exfiltrated (e.g., via SQL injection or path traversal) [verified: Passwords hashed with unsalted MD5 (hashlib.md5) which is trivially susceptible to brute-force and rainbow-table attacks.]

Login credentials exposed to console/logs via print() — Anyone with access to application logs (stdout/container logs) can read plaintext usernames and passwords of every user who logs in [verified: print(content) at /login writes the full JSON including password to stdout, which Tornado captures in application logs.]

Insecure Direct Object Reference on Customer Data Endpoints — Cross-tenant / cross-user data access: any authenticated user can enumerate and exfiltrate all customer records (PII, emails, credit cards) [verified: No ownership or authorization check on customer ID; any authenticated user can query any customer record via /fetch/customer or /get/<cust_id>.]

Credit Card Numbers Exposed in Customer API Responses — Exposure of PCI-regulated financial data (credit card numbers) to any authenticated user, severe compliance violation (PCI DSS) and risk of financial fraud [verified: customer_record.ccn is included unmasked in JSON responses from /fetch/customer and /get/<cust_id> with no access-level filtering.]

Insecure Direct Object Reference in get_customer Endpoint — An authenticated attacker can enumerate and view all customer records by iterating numeric IDs via GET /get/<id>, accessing PII and financial data across all tenants/users. [verified: Customer.query.get(cust_id) at line 231 uses the URL path parameter directly with zero ownership or authorization checks; insecure_verify() bypasses real signature validation so any token grants access to any customer record by numeric ID.]

Credit Card Numbers Exposed in get_customer API Response — Any authenticated user can retrieve credit card numbers of all customers via GET /get/<cust_id>, causing financial data breach and PCI DSS violation. [verified: get_customer() at /get/<cust_id> returns ccn in JSON response (line 235); insecure_verify() always returns True (verify=False at line 97), so any token-holder (or anyone with any Authorization header) can retrieve any customer's credit card number with no redaction.]

Server-Side Template Injection via Search Error Handler — Remote code execution on the server, full server compromise, data exfiltration [verified: search_term reflected in SQL error str(e) is interpolated into the template via % formatting and evaluated by render_template_string; requires JWT auth but auth is freely obtainable via /register/user+/login.]

XML External Entity Injection via DOCX Upload — Server-side file disclosure (e.g., /etc/passwd, source code), internal network SSRF, denial of service via entity expansion [verified: lxml 4.2.1 resolves external entities by default and python-docx 0.8.5 does not disable this; crafted DOCX can exfiltrate files; no auth required.]

Missing Rate Limiting on User Registration Endpoint — An attacker can mass-register thousands of user accounts, exhausting disk space and database resources, or use registration as an oracle to test credentials before attacking the login endpoint. [verified: The /register/user endpoint at line 134 accepts POST requests creating user accounts with no rate limiting, CAPTCHA, or IP-based throttling, enabling automated mass registration to exhaust resources.]

Missing Rate Limiting on Customer Registration Endpoint — An attacker can mass-register fraudulent customer records containing arbitrary PII and credit card data, exhausting database storage and polluting the customer database. [verified: The /register/customer endpoint at line 146 accepts POST requests creating customer records with no rate limiting or abuse prevention, allowing bulk injection of junk PII/credit-card data.]

Missing Rate Limiting on Login Endpoint — Brute-force password guessing against all accounts, including the pre-seeded admin account (admin/admin123) [verified: No rate limiting, account lockout, or CAPTCHA on /login enabling unlimited brute-force password guessing.]

Unbounded file upload leads to disk-exhaustion DoS — Attacker exhausts server disk space, causing application crash and denial of service for all users [verified: No size validation or content-length check on uploaded files; f.save(file_path) writes directly to disk enabling disk-exhaustion DoS.]

Unbounded File Upload in yaml_hammer Leading to Disk Exhaustion — An unauthenticated attacker can upload arbitrarily large files repeatedly to fill the server's disk, causing denial of service for all users. [verified: yaml_hammer at line 324 calls f.save(file_path) with no file-size limits, content-type validation, or authentication; an unauthenticated attacker can upload arbitrarily large files repeatedly to exhaust disk space.]

JWT Token Payload Printed to Console in verify_jwt — Decoded JWT tokens containing usernames are written to stdout, exposing user identity information in server logs that may be accessible to unauthorized parties. [verified: verify_jwt at line 88 prints the decoded JWT payload (containing username) to stdout via print('JWT Token from API: {0}'.format(decoded)); user identity data leaks into console/logs.]

User Enumeration via Registration Error Messages — Attacker can determine which usernames are already registered by observing error message differences, enabling targeted credential attacks [verified: Raw exception messages (str(e.message)) expose IntegrityError details and 200 vs 404 status codes reveal whether a username already exists.]
